statement: A solid is a group or component with a finite closed volume (no missing faces, every edge shared by exactly two faces); Entity Info reports Solid status, volume and offers Solid Inspector style diagnosis.

source.ref: Solid definition and solid status check

superiority: Diagnoses and auto-repairs non-manifold, flipped and open meshes with a report.
notes: also: https://help.sketchup.com/en/sketchup/inspecting-entity Acceptance sketch: Open and closed fixtures: solid flag true only for manifold watertight groups; volume equals closed form within 1e-9 relative.

statement: Outer Shell merges overlapping solids keeping only the external faces and returns a group, reducing geometry.
superiority: Exact boolean on curved and NURBS solids.
notes: Acceptance sketch: Two overlapping boxes: result volume equals analytic union volume and has no internal faces.

statement: Union merges two or more solids into a single solid group, keeping the outer geometry and interior.
superiority: Union is order independent and non-destructive when desired.
notes: Acceptance sketch: Union of three overlapping spheres: volume by inclusion-exclusion within 1e-6 relative.

statement: Procedural Union combines solids into a procedural component, nesting each union so every part stays editable.
superiority: Procedural history is a first-class editable tree.
notes: also: https://help.sketchup.com/en/release-notes/sketchup-desktop-20270 Acceptance sketch: Edit one operand after union; result updates and volume matches new closed form.

statement: Subtract removes the second selected solid by the first (cutter) and deletes the cutter; selection order matters.
superiority: Keeps cutter optional in model as a hidden operand.
notes: Acceptance sketch: Cylinder from box: volume equals box minus cylinder within 1e-6 relative; order reversal swaps the roles.

statement: Procedural Subtract creates a procedural component preserving the target attributes while cutting.
superiority: Operand parameters exposed as drivers.
notes: also: https://help.sketchup.com/en/release-notes/sketchup-desktop-20270 Acceptance sketch: Move the cutter after subtraction; cut position updates.

statement: Trim cuts the second solid with the first and keeps the first in the model.
superiority: Same with undo and cutter retention flags.
notes: Acceptance sketch: Trim a box by a plane-bounded solid; remaining volume equals closed form, cutter unchanged.

statement: Intersect leaves only the volume shared by two solids.
superiority: Exact for surfaces of revolution.
notes: Acceptance sketch: Two cylinders: intersection volume equals closed form (Steinmetz) within tolerance.

statement: Procedural Intersect keeps the shared volume as a procedural component.
superiority: Operand history is a first-class editable tree, so any intermediate can be inspected or replaced.
notes: Acceptance sketch: Intersect two overlapping solids procedurally; move one operand and verify the result updates to the new analytic volume.

statement: Split divides overlapping solids along the intersection into separate pieces.
superiority: Piece naming and classification inheritance.
notes: Acceptance sketch: Two boxes: three pieces whose volumes sum to union volume.

statement: Solid tools are available in Tools menu, Solid Tools toolbar, Procedures toolbar and context menu with preselection.

source.ref: Solid tools via context menu and Tools menu and toolbars

superiority: Single command search entry.
notes: Acceptance sketch: All entry points produce equal results for the same selection order.

statement: Procedural solid tools preserve attributes of the target; booleans carry materials of originating faces.

source.ref: Solid tools attribute and material preservation

superiority: Attributes merge rules configurable.
notes: also: https://help.sketchup.com/en/sketchup/modeling-complex-3d-shapes-solid-tools Acceptance sketch: Boolean of two materials: result faces keep source materials.

statement: Solid operations apply to groups and components with transforms; nested solids are handled and results are groups.

source.ref: Solid tools on components with nested geometry

superiority: Handles non-uniform scale correctly.
notes: Acceptance sketch: Boolean of a nested component under a scaled parent: transformed volume correct.

statement: Web client provides a Solid Inspector that highlights and fixes problems making a model non-solid.
superiority: Desktop-native, fast on million-face models.
notes: Acceptance sketch: Fixture with 5 defect classes; each is listed and the repaired model is a solid.

statement: Copy Along places copies of a group or component along a whole path as a procedural component, with distribution by count, distance or gap.
superiority: Distribution along any curve with arc-length parameterization.
notes: Acceptance sketch: 10 copies by count along a 10 m path: spacing is path length over (n-1) within 1e-9.

statement: Copy Along each segment distributes copies per path segment with absolute or relative margin modes.
superiority: Per-segment parameter overrides.
notes: Acceptance sketch: Segments 3 m and 5 m, 2 copies each; margin applied per segment exactly.

statement: Copy Along on corners places copies at the path's corner vertices with orientation.
superiority: Corner orientation options (bisector, normal, tangent).
notes: Acceptance sketch: Rectangular path: 4 copies at corners, orientation matches corner bisector.

statement: Orientation modes yaw-only or yaw and pitch along sloping paths.

source.ref: Copy Along orientation (stairlike yaw only and roadlike yaw and pitch)

superiority: Full Frenet or user-defined up-vector frames.
notes: Acceptance sketch: Sloped path: stairlike keeps vertical axis; roadlike matches slope within 1e-9.

statement: Procedural components expose parameters in Entity Info and can be edited, nested and reused like components.

source.ref: Procedural component editing in Entity Info

superiority: Parameters are bindable to the model data graph.
notes: Acceptance sketch: Change parameters; geometry regenerates deterministically (same input, same output hash).

statement: Procedures menu and toolbar offer Copy Along, Follow Me and solid operations.
superiority: Fully customizable ribbon and command palette with search across all procedures.
notes: Acceptance sketch: Enable the Procedural Tools toolbar through View > Toolbars; restart; the toolbar state persists.
